name: Avatar
description: An avatar represents a person or team with their photo, or their initials when there’s no photo. It can show presence, and AvatarGroup stacks several with a count of the rest.
whenToUse: Next to a person’s name in lists, comments, cards and headers.
To show who is involved in something, e.g. meeting attendees (AvatarGroup).
To show someone’s presence (online, away, busy) at a glance.

whenNotToUse.text: As the only way to identify a person where names matter.
whenNotToUse.alternative: Avatar with the name as text

anatomy.name: Frame
anatomy.description: Holds the image; corners follow the radius theme.

anatomy.name: Image or initials
anatomy.description: The photo, or up to two initials when there is none or it fails to load.

anatomy.name: Status dot
anatomy.description: Optional presence indicator with a ring separating it from the photo.

values.meaning: 24px. Dense lists, table rows, stacked groups.

states.name: Initials
states.trigger: No src, or the image fails to load.

behavior.text: If the image fails to load, the avatar switches to initials automatically.
The name (and status) is announced. Set decorative when the name is already shown as text next to it.
AvatarGroup shows up to max avatars, then “+N”, announced as “and N more”.
The status dot and overlap follow the reading direction.

content: Pass the full name; initials are derived from the first two words.
Label groups with what they represent: “Meeting attendees”, “Project members”.

guidelines.do: Show the person’s name next to the avatar where it matters.
guidelines.dont: Rely on the photo alone to identify someone.
guidelines.why: Faces are hard to tell apart at small sizes, and missing photos fall back to initials.

guidelines.do: Mark the avatar decorative when the name is right next to it.
guidelines.dont: Let screen readers read the same name twice.
guidelines.why: Repetition makes lists slow to navigate.

guidelines.do: Limit groups with max and show the count.
guidelines.why: A few faces plus “+8” is easier to read than a crowded row.

accessibility.role: img with an aria-label (the name and status), or hidden when decorative.

keyboard.action: Not interactive. Wrap it in a link or button if it should do something.

aria.when: decorative prop, when the name is shown as text.

accessibility.focus: Avatars aren’t focusable on their own.

wcag.how: Every avatar has a text alternative (the name) or is marked decorative.
Status is also announced in words, not only shown by dot color.
Initials pass 4.5:1 on the fallback background.

notes: Status colors are not the only cue: show the status in words where it matters.

examples.title: Avatar with a photo
examples.description: Falls back to initials if the photo is missing.
examples.code:
import { Avatar } from '@ds/react';

<Avatar name="Sarah Chen" src="/avatars/sarah.png" status="online" />

examples.title: Next to a name
examples.description: Hide it from screen readers when the name is shown as text.
examples.code:
import { Avatar } from '@ds/react';
Sarah Chen

related.relation: Profile header pattern built with an xlarge Avatar.

changes: name prop (accessible name and initials) replaces alt; initials and icon fallbacks; image error fallback.
Sizes small, medium, large, xlarge; the radius prop was removed (corners follow the radius theme).
Status dot and AvatarGroup with max and a “+N” count.

components.name: Avatar
components.description: A person's or team's picture, with initials or an icon as the fallback.

name.description: The person's (or team's) name. Used as the accessible name and for the initials fallback.

src.description: Photo URL. If it's missing or fails to load, initials are shown instead.

status.description: Presence dot. Announced after the name, e.g. "Sarah Chen, Online".

statusLabel.description: Replaces the default status wording, e.g. for translation.

decorative.description:
Hides the avatar from screen readers. Use when the name is already shown as text right
next to it, so it isn't read twice.

components.name: AvatarGroup
components.description: Overlapping avatars for a set of people, with a count of the rest.

label.description: What the group represents, e.g. "Meeting attendees". Announced before the avatars.

max.description: Show at most this many avatars, then a "+N" count.

size.description: Size for every avatar in the group.

--avatar-bg-color.description: Subtle tinted background for a tone, e.g. alerts, selected items, badges.

--avatar-text-color.description: Main tone-colored text on light or tinted backgrounds: titles, active items.

--avatar-font-family.description: Body text and most UI text.

--avatar-ring-color.description: Cards, panels, inputs and menus sitting on --color-bg-default.

--avatar-status-online-color.description: Solid fill for emphasized actions of a tone, e.g. filled buttons.

--avatar-status-away-color.description: Solid fill for emphasized actions of a tone, e.g. filled buttons.

--avatar-status-busy-color.description: Solid fill for emphasized actions of a tone, e.g. filled buttons.

--avatar-status-offline-color.description: Solid fill for emphasized actions of a tone, e.g. filled buttons.

--avatar-group-gap.description: Negative space (-4px) for deliberate overlap, e.g. stacked avatars.

--avatar-small-border-radius.description: Corner radius steps in px (see --radius-* in themes/radius.css).

--avatar-medium-border-radius.description: Corner radius steps in px (see --radius-* in themes/radius.css).
